A dataset of 25 car models spanning SUVs, sedans, and electric vehicles, each rated across seven consumer-relevant performance dimensions on a normalized 0–100 scale (higher is better). Designed for multi-dimensional comparison via parallel coordinates.

- **interior_space** (integer, 42–95): Cabin and cargo volume score
- **resale_value** (integer, 35–92): Projected 5-year value retention score
- **emission_rating** (integer, 25–98): Environmental cleanliness score; electric vehicles score near-maximum

- All scores are normalized to a 0–100 scale for cross-dimension comparability

- No single model scores in the top 3 across all seven dimensions simultaneously
- Scores are illustrative estimates based on publicly available consumer review aggregates, not official test results

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    source = json.load(f)

cars = source['cars']['data']
dimensions = source['cars']['dimensions']
categories = source['cars']['categories']

# Dimension display names
dim_labels = {
    'price_score': 'Affordability\nScore',
    'fuel_efficiency': 'Fuel\nEfficiency',
    'power': 'Power',
    'safety': 'Safety',
    'interior_space': 'Interior\nSpace',
    'resale_value': 'Resale\nValue',
    'emission_rating': 'Emissions\nRating',
}

# Color palette - business professional
type_colors = {
    'SUV': '#2C5F8A',       # Deep blue
    'Sedan': '#E87722',     # Burnt orange
    'Electric': '#2E8B57',  # Sea green
}
type_alpha = 0.45
type_lw = 1.2

# Compute top performer per axis
top_performers = {}
for dim in dimensions:
    best = max(cars, key=lambda c: c[dim])
    top_performers[dim] = best

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#FAFBFB')
ax.set_facecolor('#FAFBFB')

# X positions for 7 axes
x = list(range(len(dimensions)))

# Set up axes
ax.set_xlim(0, len(dimensions) - 1)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)

# Draw horizontal gridlines
for y_val in range(0, 101, 20):
    ax.axhline(y=y_val, color='#E0E0E0', linewidth=0.6, zorder=0)

# Draw vertical axis lines
for i in range(len(dimensions)):
    ax.axvline(x=i, color='#888888', linewidth=1.2, zorder=1)

# Plot each car as a polyline
type_drawn = set()
for car in cars:
    y_vals = [car[dim] for dim in dimensions]
    ctype = car['type']
    label = ctype if ctype not in type_drawn else None
    type_drawn.add(ctype)
    ax.plot(x, y_vals,
            color=type_colors[ctype],
            alpha=type_alpha,
            linewidth=type_lw,
            marker='o',
            markersize=3.5,
            markeredgewidth=0,
            zorder=2,
            label=label)

# Highlight top performers with distinct markers
star_color = '#D32F2F'  # Red accent for highlighting
for dim, car in top_performers.items():
    dim_idx = dimensions.index(dim)
    y_val = car[dim]
    ax.scatter(dim_idx, y_val,
               marker='D',
               s=90,
               facecolor=star_color,
               edgecolor='white',
               linewidths=1.2,
               zorder=10,
               alpha=0.95)

# Add top performer labels
for dim, car in top_performers.items():
    dim_idx = dimensions.index(dim)
    y_val = car[dim]
    # Short model name
    name = car['model'].replace('Chevy ', '').replace('Ford ', '').replace('Hyundai ', '')
    if len(name) > 13:
        name = name.replace('Mustang ', '').replace('Mercedes ', '')
    ax.annotate(name,
                xy=(dim_idx, y_val),
                xytext=(0, 8),
                textcoords='offset points',
                fontsize=7.5,
                fontweight='bold',
                color=star_color,
                ha='center',
                va='bottom',
                zorder=11)

# Axis labels and ticks
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels([dim_labels[d] for d in dimensions], fontsize=10, fontweight='medium', color='#333333')
ax.set_yticks(range(0, 101, 20))
ax.set_yticklabels([str(i) for i in range(0, 101, 20)], fontsize=9, color='#555555')

# Spine cleanup
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', length=0, pad=6)

# Annotations for key pattern observations
# Power vs Fuel Efficiency trade-off crossing
ax.annotate('Power–Efficiency\ntrade-off crossing',
            xy=(2.1, 50), fontsize=8, color='#888888',
            ha='center', style='italic',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#F5F5F5', edgecolor='#CCCCCC', alpha=0.8))

# SUV space band
ax.annotate('SUV space\nband', xy=(4.1, 93), fontsize=8,
            color=type_colors['SUV'], ha='center', style='italic')

# Electric emissions band
ax.annotate('Electric\nemissions ceiling', xy=(5.9, 92), fontsize=8,
            color=type_colors['Electric'], ha='center', style='italic')

# Title and subtitle
ax.set_title('Every Car Is a Compromise: 25 Models Across 7 Dimensions',
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', color='#222222', pad=22)
ax.text(0.5, -0.06,
        'Normalized scores (0–100); higher is better. Affordability is inverted — higher score = more affordable.\n'
        'Red diamonds mark the top-scoring model on each axis. Colored bands reveal vehicle-type behavior patterns.',
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10, color='#666666', ha='center', va='top',
        style='italic')

# Legend
legend_patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=type_colors[t], alpha=0.8, label=t) for t in categories]
leg = ax.legend(handles=legend_patches,
                loc='upper right',
                fontsize=11,
                frameon=True,
                fancybox=True,
                framealpha=0.9,
                edgecolor='#DDDDDD',
                title='Vehicle Type',
                title_fontsize=11)
leg.get_frame().set_facecolor('white')

# Add axis range label
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    ax.text(i, -6, '0–100', ha='center', fontsize=7,
            color='#AAAAAA', style='italic')

plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=180, bbox_inches='tight',
            facecolor=fig.get_facecolor(), edgecolor='none')
plt.close()

print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
